newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican opposition claim foul play wrecked TV message.
newsitem.headline: Mexican opposition claim foul play wrecked TV message.

text.p: Mexico's top conservative opposition party has claimed that a live TV brodcast by their candidate for mayor of Mexico City was intentionally interfered with.

"An unjustifiable fault completely sullied (Carlos Castillo Pereza's message)," the National Action Party's National Executive Committee said in a statement on Tuesday night protesting the "clumsy way" in which the TV broadcast was interrupted.
Castillo was given a prime time slot live on several channels to put forward his programme of action if elected in key July 6 mid-term elections.
But as soon as he started talking a intermittent beep could be heard over his message making the programme difficult to hear. As soon as the programme ended, the beep stopped, viewers said.
Castillo was given the slot by the National Chamber for the Radio and Television Industries after other leading candidates for mayor of Mexico City refused to debate with him in public on May 25.
Emilio Nassar, the head of the chamber, told Reforma newspaper that the beep came from where the live message was transmitted.
"These things happen," he said, denying foul play but agreeing the message would be broadcast again on Wednesday at the same prime time hour on four channels.
The PAN leadership was adamant that dirty tricks were involved.

"The PAN considers what happened today a bad omen for the elections of July 6 and urge that the authorities explain the motive behind this shameful action that make people recall the worst anti-democractic practices of the Mexican political system," the party said.

Mexicans vote on Sunday for an entirely new congress, a quarter of senate, six state governors and, for the first time, mayor of Mexico City. Previously, the post has been hand-picked by the president.
